name: prompt-version-grain
title: Prompt Version Grain
description: Prompt version history read like woodgrain — one vertical fiber per prompt block running down through every revision, continuous where that block is unchanged and nicked where it churned, so the load-bearing parts of a prompt are visible without diffing anything.
useWhen: the panel that answers 'which parts of this prompt are load-bearing and which churn every release' across a whole version history at once — each prompt block is one vertical fiber whose unbroken length IS its stability, so a never-touched system block reads as a single 300px line and a rewritten tools block reads as a ladder of stubs. Pick diff-unified-viewer instead when the user needs the actual line-level text change between two specific versions, approval-inline-diff when a proposed edit needs accepting or rejecting, and context-prompt-shims when the user is composing what goes into the prompt rather than auditing what already happened to it.
instruction: PromptVersionGrain renders a prompt's revision history as woodgrain in a single CSS grid: columns are prompt BLOCKS (`blocks: {id,label}[]` — system, persona, tools, rules, examples, format) and rows are VERSIONS newest at the top (`versions: {id,label,tokens,score,cells}[]`, where `cells` maps blockId to `{hash, tokens, added?, removed?}` or null). Resting row height is 26px (`rowHeight`), column min-width 84px (`columnMinWidth`), so twelve releases across six blocks is a ~312px-tall field. Every cell where the block EXISTS draws a 1px vertical fiber at the column centre spanning the full row height, `var(--foreground)` at 0.55 alpha. CONTINUITY IS THE ENTIRE MECHANISM and there is no colour or hue coding anywhere: if a cell's `hash` equals the hash in the row directly BELOW it (the older version) the fiber crosses that row boundary uninterrupted, so an untouched block accumulates into one unbroken line down the whole card; if the hashes differ the boundary gets a NICK — a 1px horizontal `--foreground` mark at 0.75 alpha spanning 60% of the column width — and the fiber is inset 3px on each side of it so the grain genuinely restarts above the nick rather than merely being crossed by it; if the block is absent in that version (`null`) nothing is drawn at all, an honest gap in the wood, and a block introduced partway through the history reads as a fiber that simply stops where it was introduced (an introduction is NOT a nick — a nick requires the block to exist on both sides of the boundary). Segment length therefore encodes stability directly: a stable block is one long fiber, a churny block is a ladder of short stubs, and nothing needs a legend. Under each column header sits a mono churn readout, `nicks / (versions - 1)` as a percentage in tabular-nums. The right gutter carries one row per version, aligned to the same `grid-template-rows` string as the grain grid so the two stay locked together: version label, a 1px `--foreground` bar whose width is that version's tokens scaled to the max version, the token count and the eval score, all Geist Mono tabular-nums, with only the newest row's label and score at full `--foreground` and the rest at `--muted`. The frame is deliberately mostly empty — six 1px fibers and a scatter of nicks over a 300px-tall grid is under 4% ink coverage. AMBIENT: only the newest row's grain heads carry a 2px-wide, 3px-tall cap and a 3.4s `opacity: 0.55 -> 1` ease-in-out alternate breathe with a deterministic per-column jitter of ±200ms (`((col * 53) % 401) - 200`), marking the live edition; nothing else moves at rest. INTERACTION: hovering anywhere in a column (detected by a single bubbling `pointerover` on the grid that resolves `closest('[data-grain-col]')`, so the synthetic pointer used by the card driver wakes it exactly like a real one) widens that column's fibers 1px -> 2px and lifts them to full alpha while every other column eases to 0.16 over 200ms ease-out, and pins that column's label plus its churn percentage at full ink while the other headers drop to 0.3. Hovering or FOCUSING a nick expands the row directly BELOW that boundary from 26px to 44px on a 220ms `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)` `grid-template-rows` transition — everything above the boundary, including the nick itself, stays at exactly the same y so the pointer never loses the target and the expansion cannot oscillate, and the rows below are pushed down, never overlaid — opening a gap that exposes a mono change summary ('+38 / -12 tok · rules') built from the cell's optional `added`/`removed` fields, falling back to the signed token delta when they are absent; the summary is edge-aligned in the first and last columns so it can never escape the grid box. Pointerleave collapses the expansion and eases every column back to its 0.55 resting alpha over the same 200ms. KEYBOARD: nicks are real `<button>`s in a roving-tabindex set (exactly one has tabIndex 0), Arrow Left/Right walk to the nearest nick in an adjacent column and Arrow Up/Down to the next nick in the same column, Enter or Space pins the expansion open (`aria-expanded`) until Escape, and every nick has a spelled-out accessible name ('rules changed between v33 and v34: +38 / -12 tok · rules') plus a 2px `var(--accent)` focus-visible outline at 3px offset. Because the grain itself is a picture, the same facts are duplicated as plain text in a visually-hidden list — one line per block giving its nick count, its churn percentage and the version it was introduced in — so nothing is conveyed by geometry alone. Colours are exclusively `--foreground`, `--muted`, `--border`, `--background` and `--accent`; there is no canvas, no SVG, no dependency and no hex literal, so both themes come for free. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes the row-expansion easing, the column dim/undim transitions and the breathe animation entirely (caps sit at full opacity) — hover, nick expansion, pinning and keyboard navigation all still work, they just change state instantly. Props: `blocks`, `versions`, `rowHeight` (26), `expandedRowHeight` (44), `columnMinWidth` (84), `ariaLabel`, `className`. The component is fully controlled and holds no data of its own, only UI state for which column is hovered and which nick is hovered, focused or pinned. Demo: twelve releases of a support-triage system prompt where `system` and `format` were never touched (two unbroken full-height fibers), `persona` was rewritten twice, `tools` changed in eight of eleven boundaries and `rules` in six (two ladders), and `examples` was introduced six releases ago so its fiber stops halfway down.
